content.title: CIME & SPIE Partnered with TDF MagnifiScience Centre for "Rescue Rangers" Workshop
content.summary: Aga Khan University CIME partnered with TDF MagnifiScience Centre to host an innovative workshop known as "Rescue Rangers: Junior Doctor Adventure."

content.text: CIME partnered with TDF MagnifiScience Centre to host an innovative workshop known as "Rescue Rangers: Junior Doctor Adventure." The goal of this unique event was to be both educational and exciting, providing an opportunity for participants to develop crucial first aid skills and critical thinking abilities.

The event was a collaborative effort between SPIE, the student-led simulation society, and the CIME team. They conducted three engaging sessions at the TDF Museum, where participants enjoyed a hands-on, holistic learning experience. Every session of the workshop featured four interactive stations:
Electrocution Station: Participants learned how to handle electric currents and shocks safely.
CPR Station: Children were taught basic CPR skills with the guidance of a CPR professional.
Burn Station: Participants learned how to manage burns effectively.
Bleeding Station: Children were taught techniques to stop bleeding instantly.

The workshop served as a qualitative research tool for the education team at CIME to study parental perceptions of community-based simulations for teaching children life-saving skills. The workshop successfully combined education with excitement, leaving a lasting impact on the participants.
